questions.q: The Vinos de Pago are spread throughout Spain. In which autonomous community does the Court say they are concentrated?
questions.exp: The Court places DO Pago estates throughout Spain but concentrated in Castilla-La Mancha, which held the first of them, Dominio de Valdepusa in Toledo and Finca Élez in Albacete, both recognised in 2003. Navarra, Valencia, Castilla y León and Aragón hold the rest.

questions.q: Which climate does the Court give the País Vasco, the Basque coast where Txakoli is grown?
questions.exp: The Court calls the País Vasco moderate maritime, the same Green Spain it names for Galicia, against Murcia's warm Mediterranean. Atlantic rain and mild temperatures on the Bay of Biscay keep acidity high and alcohol low in the grapes for Txakoli.

questions.q: Why were Murcia's Monastrell vines historically left ungrafted, according to the Court?
questions.exp: The Court's Certified grape growing cell says Monastrell vines were historically ungrafted because of the sandiness of the soil. Phylloxera cannot move or survive well in loose sand, so many Jumilla vines grew on their own roots until the louse arrived in 1989.

questions.q: In what does the Court say modern Txakoli is made?
questions.exp: The Court's Certified winemaking cell for the País Vasco reads modern: temperature-controlled stainless steel tanks. Cool fermentation keeps Txakoli fresh, sharp and lightly effervescent; the same cell gives the DO Pago estates primarily international styles of red wine.

questions.q: Which white grape does the Court name for the Txakoli of the País Vasco?
questions.exp: Hondarrabi Zuri, zuri meaning white in Basque, is the Court's white grape for the País Vasco and the base of nearly all Txakoli. Its black-skinned partner Hondarrabi Beltza, beltza meaning black, gives the rare reds and rosados.

questions.q: Jumilla DO makes dry red wine focused on which grape, pure or as the base of blends?
questions.exp: The Court lists Jumilla DO in Murcia for dry red wine focused on pure Monastrell and Monastrell-based blends. The late-ripening grape, Mourvèdre in France, needs the long heat of the southeast to soften its tannin; Mencía is the red of Bierzo, Graciano a Rioja blender and Hondarrabi Beltza Basque.

questions.q: Getariako Txakolina and Bizkaiko Txakolina are two of the Court's three Txakoli DOs. Which is the third?
questions.exp: The three Txakoli DOs are named for the three Basque provinces: Getariako Txakolina in Gipuzkoa, the oldest, Bizkaiko Txakolina in Bizkaia and Arabako Txakolina in Álava, the youngest. The Court gives all three the same wine: primarily dry white, lightly effervescent, high in acidity and meant for early drinking.

questions.q: How does the Court describe the fizz of a Txakoli?
questions.exp: The Court's style cell says Txakoli is lightly effervescent with high acidity, mostly dry white with rare reds and rosados, and meant for early consumption. The prickle comes from carbon dioxide kept in the wine at bottling, and Basque bars pour it from a height to lift it.

questions.q: What unit of land does a Spanish DO Pago protect?
questions.exp: A DO Pago, or Vino de Pago, is a single estate with its own denomination, which the Court asks a candidate to define and to place in the Spanish hierarchy. Each one is a producer appellation for one property, often outside traditional styles, rather than a region that growers share.

questions.q: In which year was the Vinos de Pago category first created?
questions.exp: The Court dates the Vinos de Pago to 2003, the year of Spain's national wine law, Ley 24/2003 de la Viña y del Vino. The number of pagos has grown since the Court's count of twenty in 2022, so the founding year is the stable fact to hold.

questions.q: Until which decade did Murcia escape phylloxera, by the Court's account?
questions.exp: The Court says Murcia avoided phylloxera until the 1980s: the louse reached Jumilla in 1989, a century after it ravaged most of Europe. The replanting on rootstock that followed brought Syrah and Cabernet Sauvignon into the region beside the old ungrafted Monastrell.

questions.q: With which kind of food does the Court say Txakoli whites are traditionally served?
questions.exp: The Court pairs Txakoli whites traditionally with oily seafood: anchovies, sardines and the pintxos of the Basque coast. The wine's sharp acidity, low alcohol and light prickle cut through the oil and salt, where game, blue cheese and chocolate need more weight or sweetness.
